data.narrative:
Itera is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by hardware veterans (AJ Cooper ex-Lyft/Uber Jump, Mattis Fj\u00e4llstr\u00f6m ex-Verkada, Alex Withrow ex-Bridgewater). The company has raised $12M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched.

Of three valuation methods tested, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $12M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $30M. Peer-Median benchmarking was not feasible: while 12 same-sector peers exist, fewer than 3 qualified under same-stage or adjacent-stage filters with comparable valuation tiers. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Itera's revenue is not disclosed, precluding use of the 21.0x P/S median observed across the three public semiconductor comps.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered at $30M. The analysis rests on a single method, creating material uncertainty. Key risks include: lack of revenue visibility, insufficient narrow-set private peer data for cross-validation, and sensitivity to stage-progression assumptions. Additional revenue or customer traction data would enable multiples-based validation and tighten the range materially.
